description: Score a prompt out of 10 on the ten checks thinkhard.si uses (what to make, who it is for, background facts, length, format, what to avoid, what good looks like, an example, what to do if unsure, layout for the model). Returns which checks pass and a plain question for each one that fails. It also reads the prompt against the expert prompts in the repository: which task it is, which of that task's inputs are there (a resume, a job posting, a policy), how ready it is for that task out of 10, and the three changes that would help most. Use it to see what a prompt is missing before improving it. The prompt is read to answer and is not stored.

prompt.description: The prompt to grade (the user message).

system.description: Optional system prompt, graded together with the prompt.

target.description: The model it is for. Layout is judged for this model.

name: grade_prompt

fill.description: The user's own material from the prompt, matched to the expert prompt's blanks by name. Pass it to get_prompt as values to start from the expert prompt with these already filled in.

inputs.description: What this task needs, in the expert prompt's order.

name.description: The input's blank name in the expert prompt.

status.description: given; missing; mentioned (named but not pasted in); blank (left as {{name}}); optional (missing, and the task works without it).

match.description: How the task was found: template (the prompt started from that thinkhard.si template), sure, likely or unsure; none when the repository has no such task, and readiness then rests on the ten checks alone.

next.description: The changes expected to raise readiness most, best first, at most three.

ask.description: What to add, in plain words.

expert.description: How the expert prompt for this task handles it.

others.description: Other tasks it might be when the match is not sure, or the nearest ones when no task fits.

readiness.description: Out of 10: how ready the prompt is for this task, from the ten checks weighed for it and the inputs it needs.

slug.description: Pass it to get_prompt for the expert version.

target.description: The model it was read for.

title: Grade a prompt out of 10
